39|BACKGROUND
40|Androgen-deprivation therapy (ADT) has been the backbone of treatment for
41|metastatic prostate cancer since the 1940s. We assessed whether concomitant
42|treatment with ADT plus docetaxel would result in longer overall survival than that
43|with ADT alone.
44|METHODS
45|We assigned men with metastatic, hormone-sensitive prostate cancer to receive
46|either ADT plus docetaxel (at a dose of 75 mg per square meter of body-surface
47|area every 3 weeks for six cycles) or ADT alone. The primary objective was to test
48|the hypothesis that the median overall survival would be 33.3% longer among
49|patients receiving docetaxel added to ADT early during therapy than among pa-
50|tients receiving ADT alone.
51|RESULTS
52|A total of 790 patients (median age, 63 years) underwent randomization. After a
53|median follow-up of 28.9 months, the median overall survival was 13.6 months
54|longer with ADT plus docetaxel (combination therapy) than with ADT alone (57.6
55|months vs. 44.0 months; hazard ratio for death in the combination group, 0.61;
56|95% confidence interval [CI], 0.47 to 0.80; P<0.001). The median time to bio-
57|chemical, symptomatic, or radiographic progression was 20.2 months in the com-
58|bination group, as compared with 11.7 months in the ADT-alone group (hazard
59|ratio, 0.61; 95% CI, 0.51 to 0.72; P<0.001). The rate of a prostate-specific antigen
60|level of less than 0.2 ng per milliliter at 12 months was 27.7% in the combination
61|group versus 16.8% in the ADT-alone group (P<0.001). In the combination group,
62|the rate of grade 3 or 4 febrile neutropenia was 6.2%, the rate of grade 3 or 4
63|infection with neutropenia was 2.3%, and the rate of grade 3 sensory neuropathy
64|and of grade 3 motor neuropathy was 0.5%.
65|CONCLUSIONS
66|Six cycles of docetaxel at the beginning of ADT for metastatic prostate cancer re-
67|sulted in significantly longer overall survival than that with ADT alone. (Funded by
68|the National Cancer Institute and others; ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT00309985.)

6|cancer were first documented in the 1940s
7|and were achieved with surgical castra-
8|tion; subsequently, androgen-deprivation therapy
9|(ADT) became the mainstay of therapy.1 Attempts
10|to improve the efficacy or decrease the treatment
11|burden of ADT have included the use of anti
12|androgens alone, intermittent dosing of ADT,
13|and the use of an antiandrogen combined with
14|medical or surgical castration.2-4 A meta-analysis
15|revealed an increase in survival of 3 percentage
16|points at 5 years with concurrent use of a non-
17|steroidal antiandrogen at the time of initiation
18|of ADT.2 However, resistance to ADT occurs in
19|most patients, with the result that the median
20|survival among patients with metastatic prostate
21|cancer is approximately 3 years.5,6 In patients
22|with resistance to ADT, docetaxel therapy re-
23|sulted in a median survival that was approxi-
24|mately 2.5 months longer than that with mito-
25|xantrone and prednisone.7,8
26|Prior studies of chemotherapy plus ADT, which
27|did not show a benefit, were small studies that
28|involved primarily patients with a relatively low
29|tumor burden.9,10 Definitions of a high burden of
30|disease have included the presence of visceral
31|metastases, a bone-metastasis burden categorized
32|by site (beyond the axial skeleton) or by a high
33|number of lesions, or a combination of these.9,11,12
34|In this study, the E3805 study, patients received
35|ADT alone or ADT plus docetaxel at the begin-
36|ning of ADT for metastatic hormone-sensitive
37|prostate cancer, and stratification was performed
38|prospectively according to high or low burden of
39|metastatic disease.
40|Methods
41|Study Oversight
42|The primary objective of the E3805 study was to
43|determine whether docetaxel therapy at the be-
44|ginning of ADT for metastatic hormone-sensitive
45|prostate cancer would result in longer overall
46|survival than that with ADT alone. The study was
47|designed in 2005 by the Eastern Cooperative On-
48|cology Group (ECOG; now part of ECOG-ACRIN)
49|and was approved by the institutional review
50|board at each participating institution. The study
51|was coordinated by the ECOG-ACRIN Cancer
52|Research Group. The ECOG-ACRIN Statistical
53|Center collected the data and was the leading
54|cooperative group and data coordinating center.
55|The first two authors attest that the study was
56|conducted and monitored as specified by the
57|protocol. The first author wrote the first draft of
58|the manuscript, with subsequent contributions
59|by all the coauthors. The authors vouch for the
60|accuracy and completeness of the data presented.
61|The protocol with the statistical analysis plan
62|is available with the full text of this article at
63|NEJM.org. Sanofi donated the docetaxel for
64|early use (i.e., before progression during ADT)
65|and provided a grant to ECOG-ACRIN but had
66|no role in the design of the protocol, the collec-
67|tion or analysis of the data, or the preparation of
68|the manuscript.
69|Patients
70|Patients were enrolled by ECOG-ACRIN, the
71|Southwest Oncology Group, the Alliance for
72|Clinical Trials in Oncology, and NRG Oncology
73|(a merged group that includes the National Sur-
74|gical Adjuvant Breast and Bowel Project, the Ra-
75|diation Therapy Oncology Group, and the Gyne-
76|cologic Oncology Group) and through the Clinical
77|Trials Support Unit. Eligible patients had a
78|pathological diagnosis of prostate cancer or a
79|clinical scenario consistent with prostate cancer
80|with an elevated prostate-specific antigen (PSA)
81|level; radiologic evidence of metastatic disease;
82|and an ECOG performance-status score of 0, 1,
83|or 2 (on a scale from 0 to 5, with higher scores
84|indicating greater disability; patients with a score
85|of 2 were eligible if the decrement in function-
86|ing was due to prostate cancer). Prior adjuvant
87|ADT was allowed if the duration of therapy was
88|24 months or less and progression had occurred
89|more than 12 months after completion of ther-
90|apy. Patients who were receiving ADT for meta-
91|static disease were eligible if there was no evidence
92|of progression and treatment had commenced
93|within 120 days before randomization. Organ
94|function that was adequate for docetaxel treat-

96|protocol). All patients provided written informed
97|consent in accordance with institutional and

24|No dose modifications of ADT were allowed,
25|and the use of a nonsteroidal antiandrogen with
26|castration (medical or surgical) at the time of

38|version 4.0 thereafter). Details on dosing are
39|provided in the protocol. If a dose was reduced
40|owing to toxic effects, it was not increased sub-
41|sequently, and docetaxel was discontinued if
42|administration was delayed longer than 3 weeks
43|from the scheduled day of dosing. The use of
44|growth factors was at the discretion of the inves-
45|tigator.
46|Monitoring of Toxic Effects and Efficacy
47|Patients assigned to combination therapy were
48|seen every 3 weeks during the period of docetaxel
49|administration and then every 3 months. Patients
50|assigned to ADT alone were seen every 3 months.
51|For the reporting of serious adverse events to the
52|NCI and to guide dose modifications, CTCAE
53|version 3.0 was used until September 2011, at
54|which time the study began using version 4.0. To
55|ensure consistency, case-report forms for toxic
56|effects that were recorded in the study database
57|retained the use of version 3.0. All grade 3 or
58|higher toxic effects in the combination group
59|were captured, and an attribution of relatedness
60|to study therapy was made by the local investiga-
61|tors. Adverse events among patients assigned to
62|ADT alone were not routinely documented, al-
63|though major adverse events were to be reported.
64|PSA levels were measured at each scheduled
65|visit. Imaging (computed tomography [CT] of
66|the abdomen and pelvis, technetium-99m bone
67|scanning, and radiography or CT of the chest)
68|was performed at baseline and at the time of
69|documented castration resistance or as clinically
70|indicated. Disease progression on imaging was

72|Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST), version 1.013
73|(the criteria are summarized in the protocol). A
74|complete serologic response was defined as a

76|consecutive measurements at least 4 weeks apart.
77|Serologic progression was defined as an increase
78|in the PSA level of more than 50% above the

81|The date of a first recorded increase of more
82|than 50% above the nadir was deemed the date

Proposal Review is ready for CHAARTED.

Selected result: time to clinical progression, from randomization, comparing ADT plus docetaxel vs ADT alone:

- HR 0.61 (95% CI 0.50–0.75)

- Proposed relation: narrower than the requested PFS outcome because death was not explicitly included in the article’s endpoint definition.
- Trial design: individually randomized parallel-group RCT; intention-to-treat analysis.

Please approve this proposal to continue the five-domain RoB 2 assessment.
